title: Extension platform: sealed Wasm extensions (WIT 2.0) with governance, an integration bus, authoring tools and an in-app Extensions UI
description: Makes the extension surface the way capabilities plug into FractalEngine. Third-party extensions ship as sealed .hexon packages (HexonType::Plugin; OD-9 closed) carrying a Wasm component bound to WIT fractalengine:plugin@2.0 through component-model bindgen. The plugin worker drives on_tick on a declared cadence budget and flushes each instance's writes (transforms, properties, readings) as ONE DbCommand::PluginCommit per tick. A host-brokered integration bus (D-X6) serves host streams (guarded query, readings, node changes, admission) and extension-declared streams, commands and hooks under capability checks. Governance builds on plugin_host_revival (signed packages, trust roots, consent, signed revocation list) and adds a per-verse install policy, ordered activation preconditions, op-log audit, kill-switch layers and host-stamped provenance. The track also adds the fe-ext authoring CLI, a Rust guest SDK, two examples, an in-app Extensions UI with a pluggable registry endpoint behind S-REGISTRY, first-party migrations (fe-sim fleets first, then device adapters, the hexon registry client and BI connectors), and scripted-simulator QA across peers. Author-only until the build gate opens (D-X2). Open capability only: no catalogue operations and no payment code.

Serves the roadmap's primary analytics persona (device adapters, BI connectors) and its platform persona (fleets, authoring). Any party may build catalogues, review or counter-signing on these seams; this repo never names or depends on such consumers.

Only the relay (spawn_api_thread) keeps the direct path. The city-lite 'reading write timed out (db thread)' replies come from that fallback (iot.rs:232).

tripwires: No cargo, rustc or simulator run while .omc/state/build-gate.json has cargo_allowed=false (D-X2). BUILD slices wait for 'gate open' on the bus and post 'building' before any build.
Entries ending in '/**' own every file under that directory, existing or future; expand them before any collision proof.
HEAD moved twice during authoring (30163ca2 -> cfd7fce6) under live P2P commits; re-verify every owns list against HEAD before launching any slice.
WIT 2.0 carries an 'UNSTABLE - not yet bound' header until E1 binds it; every later WIT edit gets a matching host change (plugin_host_revival tripwire).
A Wasm guest never holds a socket, file handle, clock source or SQL string; an import that hands one over is a defect.
One flush per instance per tick: a diff that adds a per-sample DB-thread command (transform, reading or derived route property) is a defect, not a tuning choice.
Extensions write only as the host's local DID through the typed bridge (no ElevatedQuery, RawQuery or caller SQL); only the local DID may install, consent, bind, update or uninstall.
An empty scope list in manifest v2 grants nothing; '*' must be explicit.
The SimClock HLC override never enters a production process; live fleets run on the wall clock.
Package loading stays default-off (plugin_host_revival OD-4) until its S6 security review passes and a decision flips it; the unsigned dev path is unreachable from release builds.
Provenance is host-stamped; the guest can neither set nor strip it. R24 withdrawal waits for OD-E1.

PUBLIC repo: no business-logic, account, payment or catalogue-operations wording in any file; registry access only through S-REGISTRY / S-ENTITLEMENT; the private side is never named. Run the staged-diff leak grep before every commit.
Tests: extend or swap journeys; new journey files only for the new public seams listed in plan §1.
Agents never run cargo; the session inks once per wave.
